skill.name: ru
skill.description: Guides the RU repo updater for syncing many GitHub repositories, planning AI reviews, and processing dirty working trees.
skill.summary: Coordinate multi-repo Git synchronization and AI-assisted review workflows with RU.
skill.author: Dicklesworthstone

security_audit.summary: Most static hits are Markdown examples or documentation text, so they are false positives for executable backtick, filesystem, token, and sensitive-file access. The audit confirms the remote install command that pipes raw GitHub content to bash, and it adds semantic risks for high-impact automated repo changes, hook execution, and warning-only secret scanning.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is piped directly to bash.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the one-line installer with download, checksum verification, source review, and an explicit local execution step.

remediation.issue: Agent workflows can commit, push, tag, and release across repositories.
remediation.suggestion: Require human confirmation before staging, committing, pushing, tagging, or creating releases, especially in parallel workflows.

remediation.issue: Per-repo hook fields can execute project-controlled commands.
remediation.suggestion: Disable hooks by default for untrusted repos, or run them only after explicit review inside a sandbox.

remediation.issue: Secret scanning defaults to warning mode.
remediation.suggestion: Make blocking mode the documented default for any workflow that can commit, push, tag, or release.

semantic_findings.title: Autonomous Repository Modification Workflow
semantic_findings.description: The skill describes agent-sweep workflows that stage files, create commits, push approved changes, tag releases, and create GitHub releases. This can modify many repositories if run without strict confirmation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documented workflow explicitly includes processing dirty repos, staging files, committing, pushing, tagging, and releasing. This is a clear high-impact automation risk even though it is described as normal RU behavior.

semantic_findings.title: Repository-Controlled Hook Execution
semantic_findings.description: The per-repo configuration example includes pre_hook and post_hook command strings. If RU executes these hooks from untrusted repositories, project-controlled configuration can run shell commands.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The YAML example shows executable hook fields, but the implementation is not included. The risk is credible because the skill presents these hooks as RU configuration.

semantic_findings.title: Secret Scanning Defaults to Warning Mode
semantic_findings.description: The secret scanning options document warn as the default and block as optional. Warning-only detection can allow risky commits or pushes unless users explicitly choose blocking.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documentation states that warn mode is default and that later phases can create commits and optionally push. The implementation may add protections, but the documented default is weaker than safe publication guidance.

dangerous_patterns.title: Pipe to shell pattern
dangerous_patterns.confidence_reasoning: Line 481 recommends piping a remote installer from raw GitHub directly into bash. This is a classic remote code execution installation pattern and should be blocked until replaced.

content.value_statement: Large GitHub workspaces are hard to keep synchronized and reviewed. This skill explains RU workflows for sync, review planning, agent sweeps, and diagnostics.
actual_capabilities: Explains RU sync, status, add, remove, prune, doctor, and self-update commands.
Describes review planning and application workflows for issues and pull requests.
Documents agent-sweep phases for planning, committing, and release preparation.
Shows configuration paths, repo list formats, layout modes, and environment variables.
Summarizes output formats, exit codes, troubleshooting steps, and rate limit behavior.
Lists quality gates and integrations with ntm and Flywheel tools.
limitations: It documents RU behavior but does not include the RU Bash implementation.
It can guide commands that change repositories, so users must review actions before applying them.
It depends on installed tools such as git, gh, tmux, ntm, jq, and RU.
It does not verify remote installer contents or external repository trust.

use_cases.title: Synchronize a Large Workspace
use_cases.description: Run read-only checks, dry runs, and controlled syncs across many configured repositories.

use_cases.title: Plan Cross-Repo Reviews
use_cases.description: Prioritize issues and pull requests, then create isolated worktrees for review sessions.

use_cases.title: Process Dirty Repositories
use_cases.description: Use agent-sweep phases to inspect changes, prepare commits, and gate release steps.

prompt_templates.title: Check Workspace Status
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the RU skill to show me a read-only status workflow for all configured repositories. Include JSON output only if useful.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Safe Sync
prompt_templates.prompt: Use RU to create a dry-run sync plan for my repositories. Explain which commands are read-only and which commands may change files.

prompt_templates.title: Review Issues Across Repos
prompt_templates.prompt: Use RU review planning to prioritize open issues and pull requests across my repos. Include cost controls and skip-day settings.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Controlled Agent Sweep
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an RU agent-sweep workflow for dirty repositories with confirmation before staging, committing, pushing, or releasing. Require secret-scan blocking.

output_examples.input: I need to sync 40 repos without changing anything yet.
output: Start with a status check and a dry-run sync.
Review skipped, diverged, and dirty repositories before applying changes.
Only run a real sync after confirming the repo list and update strategy.

output_examples.input: Plan an AI review sweep with a small budget.
output: Limit the number of repositories and runtime first.
Prioritize security, critical, bug, and recently updated items.
Use isolated worktrees and apply changes only after human review.

output_examples.input: Help me process dirty repos safely.
output: Generate an agent-sweep plan before applying it.
Block secret findings and deny sensitive file patterns.
Require confirmation before commits, pushes, tags, or releases.

best_practices: Start with read-only status checks, dry runs, and explicit repo filters.
Use secret-scan blocking before any commit, push, tag, or release workflow.
Review agent plans and quality gate results before applying changes.
anti_patterns: Do not run remote installer scripts through a shell without inspecting them first.
Do not let agent-sweep push or release changes without human confirmation.
Do not run hooks from untrusted repositories without sandboxing or review.

faq.question: What is RU?
faq.answer: RU is a repo updater workflow for syncing many GitHub repositories and coordinating AI-assisted reviews.

faq.question: Does this skill include the RU program?
faq.answer: No. It documents commands, workflows, configuration, outputs, and safety practices for an external RU CLI.

faq.question: Can it change repositories?
faq.answer: Yes, some workflows can stage, commit, push, tag, or release. Use dry runs and confirmations first.

faq.question: Which tools does it expect?
faq.answer: It references git, gh, curl, jq, tmux, ntm, Claude Code, and the RU command.

faq.question: How should secrets be handled?
faq.answer: Use denylist rules and set secret scanning to block before any push or release action.

faq.question: Is the one-line installer safe?
faq.answer: It uses a remote script piped to a shell. Inspect the script before running any installation command.
